html:
SMTO-EXE-0029 — SMTO couldn't open the folder for this command

GUID: 1c3fe5bd-7cb9-4591-b022-3e806fb87770
Slug: working-directory-inaccessible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run a command inside a folder, but couldn't open that folder on the computer. The command did not run, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and note the folder path. Check that this folder exists on the computer running the Gateway and is spelled exactly the same. The command runs on the Gateway's computer, so the folder must exist there, not only on your own computer.
  2. Make sure the user account that runs the Gateway is allowed to open that folder and each folder above it. Ask that computer's owner to allow access to that folder only. If any folder along the way is locked, SMTO can't get into it.
  3. In the conversation, tell SMTO the exact folder to use, then ask it to run the step again. The command never started, so running it again is safe once the folder can be opened.

What success looks like

  • The step starts and shows the command's output instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't give everyone full access to the folder to get past this; grant only the access the Gateway needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested working directory could not be resolved or accessed on the execution host (OSError, ValueError or RuntimeError during path resolution), so the command was not started.

What this means

  • Resolving or accessing the requested working directory raised an OS, value or path-resolution error, distinct from a proven missing-directory/type check. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Resolving or accessing the requested working directory raised an OS, value or path-resolution error, distinct from a proven missing-directory/type check.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the target-local resolved path and retained exception category, including traversal permissions and link resolution.

How to fix it

  • Read the cwd in the failed-to-start receipt (error_kind invalid_working_directory) and check on the selected Gateway host that the path resolves and that the Gateway's OS account has traverse (execute) permission on every parent directory (gateway_core.paths.resolve_gateway_execution_cwd; agent_runtime.execution.paths.resolve_cwd). Choose an accessible directory, or grant only the exact access needed.
  • Inspect the exact path on the selected Gateway and its traversal permissions. Choose an accessible directory; change permissions only when authorized.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorized directory can be resolved and accessed on the selected execution host.

What not to do

  • Do not grant broad permissions; verify the exact resource, identity and required access.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
